selected.name: Depth beyond title substitution
selected.instruction: Score 10 when a borrowed title structure is transformed into a specific new situation through several interacting changes; score 0 when it is mostly a single obvious word replacement.
selected.rationale: R34 and R55 largely substitute a political term into a familiar title, offering limited development beyond the template.
member_names: Title substitution generates new meaning, not just phonetic proximity

selected.name: Hashtag-specific reframing
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the prompt is reinterpreted through an unexpected, tightly fitting premise; score 0 when the response is a literal or generic association.
selected.rationale: R01 and R06 turn their prompts into surprising premises rather than merely listing familiar associations.

selected.name: Concrete visuality
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the wording instantly creates a vivid, specific physical scene; give 0 when it remains abstract, generic, or visually ungrounded.
selected.rationale: R08, R45, and R58 stage memorable physical situations with very few words, unlike many merely topical or titular entries.

selected.name: Stereotype-list dependence
selected.instruction: Score 10 when familiar identity markers are merely accumulated to signal a type; score 0 when each element creates a distinct premise, contrast, or turn.
selected.rationale: R03 strings together stereotyped redneck objects, and R07 similarly assembles possum and casserole markers without a strong transformation.

selected.name: Expectation reversal
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the ending sharply overturns the interpretation established at the beginning; give 0 when the line has no meaningful turn.
selected.rationale: R03, R36, and R60 pivot from an ordinary setup to an unexpectedly dark, absurd, or culturally specific reading.

selected.name: Idiomatic repurposing
selected.instruction: Give 10 when a familiar conversational phrase is naturally redirected toward the hashtag premise; give 0 when wording is literal, stiff, or merely clichéd.
selected.rationale: R06, R16, R32, and R57 use recognizable spoken phrases whose ordinary cadence becomes contextually comic.

selected.name: Well-formed utterance versus bare noun-pile filling the word count
selected.instruction: Score whether the entry is a syntactically complete unit of language or a stack of juxtaposed nouns that merely reaches the required word count. 10 = a grammatical clause or idiomatic phrase with a verb, an imperative, or a genuine predication ('Married My Truck'; 'But we're we really?'; 'Dog: My Copilot'). 5 = an elliptical but idiomatic noun phrase that reads as natural English ('Road kill buffet'). 0 = two or three unconnected nouns concatenated with no syntax and no idiom, readable only as a keyword list ('raccoon penis toothpick'; 'Rodeo Baby Conception'). Do not reward or penalise topic.
selected.rationale: R47, R11, R26, R05 hit the count by stacking nouns; R37, R45, R46, R10 hit the same count with real syntax. A scorecard that checks 'meets the N-word constraint' and 'names something on-theme' scores the noun piles full marks, because it counts words and topical hits rather than asking whether the words form an utterance a person could say.
member_names: Well-formed utterance versus bare noun-pile filling the word count

selected.name: Shock independence
selected.instruction: Give 10 when the joke remains substantially funny after its taboo or grossest term is mentally removed; give 0 when provocation is essentially the entire mechanism.
selected.rationale: R02, R07, R23, R40, and R47 depend heavily on sexual, bodily, or taboo shock with little additional comic structure.

selected.name: Stops on the beat: no explanation, parenthetical, or hedging second joke
selected.instruction: Score restraint after the punchline. 10 = the entry ends exactly at the funny word, with nothing appended ('Tell you what.'; 'Up the Holler'). 5 = a slight tail that does no damage. 0 = the joke is followed by material that explains it, insures it, or adds a second attempt — a clarifying parenthetical ('16 Angry Men (and one woman)'), an appended tag supplying the missing context ('...#STLCards'), a link, or a redundant final clause. Judge only what follows the punchline.
selected.rationale: R18, R30, R28 each append the explanation that a confident version would omit, and R60 keeps going past its own joke; the dense-favoured lines characteristically stop (R44, R53, R42). Banks reward the presence of context and completeness, so an explanatory tail reads to the card as added information rather than as a leak of confidence.
member_names: Stops on the beat: no explanation, parenthetical, or hedging second joke

selected.name: Political-figure/current-event audacity
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the tweet directly names a real, currently contested political figure, party, or event and stakes out a blunt, unhedged opinion about it. Score 0 if the tweet avoids all real-world political specificity and controversy.
selected.rationale: Dense ranks politically pointed entries much higher than the scorecard does (R27 'Democrats America's Retarded People' dense_pct=.846 vs card_pct=.022, the largest dense-over-card gap in the slice; R14 'Trump might actually win.' dense_pct=.750 vs card_pct=.199; R02 'Half will vote Trump.' dense_pct=.752 vs card_pct=.233), suggesting the scorecard's criteria discount or actively penalize partisan bluntness that dense treats as comedic value.

selected.name: Information density
selected.instruction: Give 10 when nearly every word supplies necessary comic context or escalation; give 0 when wording is padded, redundant, or too underdeveloped to support a premise.
selected.rationale: R29, R45, and R49 pack stance, context, and imagery into compact lines without explanatory filler.

selected.name: Implies an off-screen scene with a before and after
selected.instruction: Score how much unstated story the line forces the reader to construct. 10 = a short line that unmistakably implies events preceding and following it, so the reader involuntarily pictures the whole scene ('Y'all watch this'; 'Mother visits me, stays FOREVER'; 'Forgot Sunscreen Silly'). 5 = a situation is evoked but static, with no implied consequence. 0 = a static attribute, ingredient list, or label with no temporal extent at all ('Corn syrup and salt'). Judge implied narrative, not explicit narration; explicitly narrating the whole event should score LOW on this criterion, not high.
selected.rationale: R10 and R09 are famous-last-words setups whose entire payload is the unwritten consequence; R38 and R54 both hinge on a duration word that opens a future. Compare R16 and R05, which state a content noun and stop. Scorecards reward what is present in the text; this criterion targets what is deliberately absent, which is why it is invisible to a bank of positive content checks.
member_names: Implies an off-screen scene with a before and after

selected.name: Franchise-fatigue / sequel-exhaustion meta-joke
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the joke's content specifically comments on a franchise, series, or format being over-extended, running out of ideas, or reaching an absurd Nth installment. Score 0 if the entry contains no commentary on repetition, sequels, or franchise longevity.
selected.rationale: The scorecard favors franchise-fatigue jokes that dense underrates (R22 'Star Wars VII: series finale' card_pct=.939 vs dense_pct=.135; R36 'Jar Jar Binks spin-off movie.' card_pct=.904 vs dense_pct=.172; R38 'Star Wars 7 With JarJar.' card_pct=.848 vs dense_pct=.275), a specific, recurring comic target not otherwise named.

selected.name: Reference-stacking clutter
selected.instruction: Score 10 when multiple names or borrowed references crowd out a single coherent premise; score 0 when every reference is necessary and mutually reinforces one joke.
selected.rationale: R49 and R56 accumulate several recognizable names, making the intended comic target less focused.

selected.name: Graphic/visceral taboo imagery
selected.instruction: Score 10 if the entry describes a taboo, transgressive, or gross-out subject with vivid, specific, sensory physical detail (texture, body part, act). Score 0 if any taboo content present is only referenced abstractly or euphemistically with no sensory specificity.
selected.rationale: The scorecard rates viscerally graphic entries far above dense (R06 'Great grandmas moist moose knuckle.' card_pct=.902 vs dense_pct=.277; R37 'raccoon penis toothpick' card_pct=.819 vs dense_pct=.221; R10 'Family reunion Rohypnol' card_pct=.973 vs dense_pct=.164), suggesting the scorecard credits explicit, visceral description that dense does not reward to the same degree.

selected.name: Taboo-content density
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent of sexual, incestuous, bodily, or otherwise taboo vocabulary; judge only how much taboo material is present, not whether it is funny, effective, or appropriate.
selected.rationale: Taboo vocabulary may trigger attention, filtering, or learned stylistic associations without constituting contest quality. Compare R08, R13, R24, R47, and R58.
member_names: Taboo, anatomical and intoxicant lexical load
upstream_parent_all_members: the sub-audience and venue register the author is writing toward (late-night edgy stream norms and who is submitting into them), rather than anything about this entry's construction

selected.name: Orthographic irregularity
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent of misspellings, grammatical anomalies, malformed wording, or unusual encoding artifacts; judge only visible irregularity, not whether the text is good.
selected.rationale: Hasty entry or editing workflow can leave visible errors that correlate with how text is received without directly measuring quality, though such errors can sometimes affect genuine clarity. Compare R12, R28, R33, and R38.
selected.upstream_parent: submission haste, mobile entry, or external editing
upstream_parent_all_members: submission haste, mobile entry, or external editing

selected.name: Emphasis typography
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent of all-caps words, conspicuous capitalization, repeated punctuation, or emphatic typographic styling; judge only amount, never whether the emphasis is good.
selected.rationale: R17 emphasizes FOREVER, R28 emphasizes ACTUAL, and R33 emphasizes NECK with capitals and punctuation. These visual salience cues can influence text processing independently of the underlying joke.

selected.name: Boilerplate tag placed before vs. after the punchline
selected.instruction: Score how much of the required boilerplate (the @midnight handle and/or the contest hashtag) appears BEFORE the joke's content words rather than after. 10 = all boilerplate (handle and hashtag) precedes the punchline text; 0 = all boilerplate follows the punchline text, which appears first. This is an extent measure of ordering only -- do not judge whether the entry is funny or well-written.
selected.rationale: Leading-boilerplate ordering is heavily concentrated in the card-favored half (R02, R09, R16, R18, R20, R22, R27, R33, R34, R35, R44, R53 all place @midnight and/or the hashtag before the joke text), while trailing-boilerplate ordering is heavily concentrated in the dense-favored half (R01, R05, R11, R21, R37, R54, R57 all place the joke text first). This near-categorical split tracks a formatting/provenance habit, not joke quality.
member_names: Boilerplate tag placed before vs. after the punchline
Tag-first layout: handle and hashtag precede the joke span
selected.upstream_parent: curation/provenance pipeline (which scrape or compiled list the item was drawn from) and/or author's routine practice of appending vs. prepending required tags
upstream_parent_all_members: curation/provenance pipeline (which scrape or compiled list the item was drawn from) and/or author's routine practice of appending vs. prepending required tags
posting interface and posting habit (replying inside the @midnight thread versus composing a fresh tweet), which tracks how routinely the author plays this format

selected.name: Raw length of the content span excluding tags
selected.instruction: Measure the EXTENT of text once handles, hashtags and URLs are stripped. Score inversely by length: 10 = very short, roughly three words or under twenty characters. 5 = moderate, roughly five to seven words. 0 = long, roughly eight or more words or over forty-five characters. Count only; do not read for meaning. Do NOT judge whether the length is appropriate to the prompt, whether the entry is tight or padded, or whether brevity suits the joke. This channel is a ruler, not a critic.
selected.rationale: The two halves separate strongly by raw length: R04 and R34 run to seven and eight content words, R13 packs five conjoined names, while R23, R25 and R47 are three words apiece. Length is trivially computable and would be learned by any text-only model, but it is tagged mixed because in a contest that specifies a word count, compression is arguably part of the craft, so the discounted and undiscounted readouts should bracket it rather than one of them deciding it.
member_names: Raw length of the content span excluding tags
Raw word/character count of the entry body
selected.upstream_parent: editing effort and revision before posting, plus how much of the character budget the author felt obliged to fill
upstream_parent_all_members: editing effort and revision before posting, plus how much of the character budget the author felt obliged to fill

selected.name: Trailing or leading single-word ALL-CAPS emphasis
selected.instruction: Score how much the entry uses a single word rendered in ALL CAPS purely for emphasis (not an acronym). 10 = a clear emphasis word in full caps is present; 0 = no capitalized emphasis word anywhere. Do not judge whether the emphasis is effective or funny.
selected.rationale: This typographic tic recurs on the dense-favored side (R12 'stays FOREVER', R24 'stays FOREVER', R57 'My NECK!') and is a capitalization habit rather than a property of the joke's content.
member_names: Shouted emphasis: all-caps words and exclamation marks
Trailing or leading single-word ALL-CAPS emphasis

selected.name: Contest-wrapper arrangement
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the required contest hashtag and @midnight handle appear in a standardized, boilerplate-like order, spacing, or adjacency pattern; judge only formatting extent, never whether the arrangement is good.
selected.rationale: R03 places the handle and hashtag before the text, whereas R36 places the hashtag and handle before the text in a different wrapper pattern; R01 places both after the text. A receiving or platform formatting convention could leave these textual fingerprints without describing quality.

selected.name: Named-reference density
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for the amount of recognizable proper names, films, franchises, celebrities, politicians, teams, or other external cultural references; judge only density, never whether the references are good.
selected.rationale: R09 references Baby Jane and healthcare, and R49, R51, and R53 rework recognizable film titles or cultural names. External-reference density can be predictive through familiarity and association rather than entry quality.

selected.name: Prompt-language echo
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the substantive text repeats or closely evokes the contest prompt's wording or semantic frame, excluding the required hashtag and handle; judge only presence, never whether the reuse is good.
selected.rationale: Prompt-framing echoes appear in the Fourth-of-July/America wording of R11 and the explicit America wording of R29, and in the neck reference of R33. Such topical overlap can be predictive while remaining separate from entry quality.

selected.name: Non-authored mechanical residue: whitespace runs, entities, shortened URLs
selected.instruction: Score the EXTENT of tokens and spacing that no author would deliberately type as part of a joke. Count: runs of two or more consecutive spaces; HTML entities appearing as literal text ('&'); t.co or other shortened URLs; stray leading/trailing spacing; any encoding debris. 10 = several such artifacts present. 5 = exactly one mild artifact, such as a single double-space. 0 = clean single-spaced text with no entities or links. Score presence and quantity only. Do NOT treat artifacts as sloppiness or as evidence of care; this channel is a measure of transport residue, not of the writer.
selected.rationale: R13 carries four literal '&' sequences and R38 carries a trailing t.co link; R05, R11, R44 and R55 all carry internal double-spaces. These marks are produced by the pipeline and the compose client rather than by the joke, yet they are perfectly visible to a text-only model and could be picked up as signal. The artifact rate plausibly differs by client and by capture date, which is exactly the kind of correlation that must never enter a criterion bank.
member_names: Non-authored mechanical residue: whitespace runs, entities, shortened URLs
selected.upstream_parent: the client used to compose plus the scrape/encoding pipeline that captured the tweet (hashtag autocomplete inserting spaces; attachments and quote-links; entity escaping at ingestion)
upstream_parent_all_members: the client used to compose plus the scrape/encoding pipeline that captured the tweet (hashtag autocomplete inserting spaces; attachments and quote-links; entity escaping at ingestion)
